label: The problem
show: Five dots, one turns amber. A bar: 4 in 10 get treatment. Then thin lines that slip down over weeks and fade.
text: One in five American teenagers goes through depression in a year, and most get no treatment. It builds slowly: a little less sleep, fewer texts, dropped plans. Nobody sees it coming, and nobody knows when to ask.

label: What we built
show: The Stability mark draws itself. Two phones slide in: Maya's and her mom's.
text: That's why we built Stability. It lives on a teenager's phone, linked to a parent's. Meet Maya.

label: Her whole digital life
show: Maya's phone in the centre. Instagram, YouTube, TikTok and browsing light up on the left; music, gaming chats and messages on the right, under '17 sources'. Then Stable floats in, drifts around, and settles into the check-in card on her phone.
text: Stability connects to her whole digital life: Instagram, YouTube, TikTok, browsing, music, gaming chats and messages. It reads it all on her phone and learns her normal. Once a week, our mascot, Stable, checks in. Two taps.

label: It asks
show: Week four: the two questions come up and she answers low. Weeks five and six: the ring turns amber, her check-ins climb, the model's score crosses its line, and the questions come up again.
text: Every month, it asks the two questions doctors use. Maya says she's mostly okay, and it takes her at her word. Then finals hit. Her check-ins get tense, and our model doesn't wait a month. It asks again.

label: The note
show: Week six she answers low again. Week eight her answers are high. Mom's phone slides in. An amber dot crosses from Maya's phone to hers and the note opens.
text: But at week eight, her answers come back high. Maya sees a nudge to see a doctor, and her mom gets a note: what changed, for how long, and how to start the conversation. Never her messages.

label: Private, with a safety net
show: Maya types a message. It becomes a bubble, then a single dot. A counter holds at 0 bytes sent. A chip: 988, one tap away.
text: Nothing she types, watches or searches ever leaves her phone. Small models read it there and keep only numbers. And if she types or searches for self-harm, 988 is one tap away.

label: The engine
show: A diagram builds: her digital life, two taps and past answers feed the engine; it opens the two questions, then the eight, then the note. Below, the two on-phone models and a lock: 0 words leave the phone.
text: Under the hood, her digital life, Stable's two taps and her past answers feed our engine. It tracks how she's doing and decides when to ask. High answers unlock the full eight questions, and only then is a parent told. No words ever leave the phone.

label: It works
show: A counter runs to 350,000+. Two bars: the ask model 44%, a fixed schedule 13%, with 3.4x. Then 0.90 on 113 teens, 92%, 2x and 13 of 15.
text: And it works. Tested on over three hundred fifty thousand real examples, our ask model finds a hard week over three times as often as a schedule. On a hundred thirteen teenagers it had never seen, it scored an AUC of point nine oh, and nine in ten of its top asks found a struggling teen. Our language models catch twice what keyword lists do.

label: Close
show: The Stability mark, 'knowing when to ask', and a small 'Prototype. Not medical advice.'
text: Stability. Knowing when to ask, so more teens get help sooner.
